title: Minimax Regret for Predicting Future Ordinal Individual Treatment Effects
banked_reason: The advertised exact finite-sample frontier remains open beyond the base case; the D0.5 reviewer graded the sound partial package incremental, below the field floor.
gap_reasons: Its advertised exact finite-sample frontier remains open beyond the base case: the contact theorem guarantees finite certificates but supplies no instantiated optimum, and the phase construction does not enumerate the phases.
The rate has nonsharp constants and no sharp local law, so it does not resolve the sampling cost at the contacts central to the question.
Solve the binary two-per-arm primal and dual to equality, then certify one size-five or size-six contact using the same coverage and regret checks.
proof_attempt_summary: Discovery established an all-rule reduction, a finite-contact representation, an exact one-per-arm value, and bounds 7/5 to 17/10 for two observations per arm. Three solve rounds did not produce the matching two-per-arm dual certificate or a certified size-five-or-six contact; oracle phase enumeration and sharp local constants also remain open. D0.5 graded the sound partial package incremental, below the field floor.
tldr: For a future realized ordinal individual effect, labelled-array exchangeability reduces randomized full-data reports to histogram mixtures. A finite-support contact representation and canonical finite oracle phase signatures are proved. Binary endpoint embedding shows \(R_J\geq J R_1\); with the plug-in/shrinkage rule this gives a two-sided \(n_{\min}^{-1/2}\) regret rate for every fixed \(J\), without excluding boundary or phase contacts. The binary base value is exact, while the two-per-arm value remains in \([7/5,17/10]\); exact instantiated contacts, complete phase enumeration, and sharp local constants remain open.
gap: Fixed-marginal Fréchet ITE theory and the screened future-ITE conformal, cluster, selection, confounding-sensitivity and continuous-covariate impossibility papers do not supply an exact two-multinomial, arbitrary-common-coupling, connected-action all-rule expected-span regret frontier. The finite-ordinal bounded-support question is outside the continuous-covariate infinite-length theorem; this is a bounded theorem-level difference, with inaccessible older theorem text disclosed.
fill: Establish the ordinal action and transport reductions, canonical phase geometry and auditable finite-contact regret representation; then obtain exact attaining rules and global dual certificates, first for binary n=2 and one binary n=5 or n=6 contact. The uniform fixed-J rate is a nonbinary consequence, and sharp contact-indexed local constants remain a further question.
